title: Canonical uniformizer scalar is preserved by geometric inverse image
statement:
Fix a prime l, a finite field extension E/Q_l and any scheme morphism f:X→Y. Let S on the internal module category of Y and T on that of X be strict presentations [def-sfb-strict-completion-restriction-data], with IsIntegral l E Y S and IsIntegral l E X T. For every module M on Y, inverse image of S.scalar_M is exactly T.scalar at the inverse image of M. No immersion or weakly etale hypothesis on f is needed for this scalar identity.

Exact Lean assertion:
theorem strictIntegralScalarPullback {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (S : Presentation.{u + 2, u + 1, u + 1} (AdicCompletion.Modules l E Y))
    (T : Presentation.{u + 2, u + 1, u + 1} (AdicCompletion.Modules l E X))
    (hS : IsIntegral l E Y S) (hT : IsIntegral l E X T)
    (M : AdicCompletion.Modules l E Y) :
    (CondensedRing.upperStar (DerivedNakayama.integerRing l E) f).map (S.scalar.app M) =
      T.scalar.app ((CondensedRing.upperStar (DerivedNakayama.integerRing l E) f).obj M)

proof.text: For canonical cone data, CoefficientCone.scalar_eq identifies both dS and dT with the same point uniformizer endomorphism. Work first with an arbitrary commutative condensed coefficient ring Λ, keeping its monoid structure as a parameter. Define the regular scalar with underlying map p_X^*(d.hom). Naturality of upperStarFromPointComp gives the coefficient scalar square. Under the extension-of-scalars adjunction, precomposition with extendUnitHom detects equality of module maps. The existing unit coherence formula identifies extendUnitHom followed by the monoidal unit with condensedPullbackHom. Thus the scalar square holds on the regular module after module inverse image. The strong monoidal left-unitor and whiskering identities give the scalar square on every module. Specialize Λ to the integer ring, and use the canonical scalar identifications to obtain the result.
